name: Deep rose red
lede: Deep rose red is a dark, muted brick-pink built by adding "deep" to [[rose-red]], and it shares its exact hex, #893843, with the unrelated library name Solid Pink.

sections.title: A modifier, not a separate color
sections.body:
Our classifier reads the name as modifier grammar: "deep" plus [[rose-red]], the same pattern as light or dark variants elsewhere in the library [1]. It carries no history of its own beyond that construction; no book or dated source in our data names a first use [1]. At lightness 35 and chroma 37, it sits well below rose-red's own brightness, closer to a dried petal than a fresh one [1].

The library's own nearest-match search lands on a different name entirely at the identical hex: [[deep-rose-red]], a separate wiki-sourced entry that happens to share #893843 to the pixel [1]. The two names are not siblings in origin, only in coordinates; the closest distinct color, once that duplicate is set aside, is [[peony-red|Peony Red]], under 3 units away by CIEDE2000 [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This exact shade covers five percent or more of the canvas in 82 of 23,781 paintings in our archive, as photographed, a rate of about 0.3 percent [2]. It is more than four times as common in Kalighat paintings and Mughal court painting than in the archive overall, and its earliest dated appearance is a 1368 Chinese portrait, *Madam Han Neefang*, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. Within its own paintings it most often sits as a mid-tone or a shadow, rarely as a highlight, and keeps company with [[mahogany|Mahogany]] and [[umber|Umber]] more than chance would predict [2].
